items.summary: Iran executes three men convicted over January 2026 protests Iran on Sunday executed three men convicted of taking part in armed unrest during protests in January 2026 and carrying out operations for Israel and the United States, state media reported. On Saturday, citing judiciary's Mizan Online website, AFP reported the execution of an Iranian,  Mohammad Aref Shahbakhsh, an "operative linked to the terrorist group Jaish al-Zolm (al-Adl)". Jaish al-Adl is an outlawed militant group in Sistan-Baluchistan province, which has long seen clashes between security forces and armed groups, including Sunni militants and members of the ethnic Baloch minority. Iran accuses arch-enemies the United States and Israel of supporting armed groups there.

items.summary: Iranian forces on higher alert, stronger than before war, spokesman says Iran's military is "stronger" and more motivated than it was when the United States and Israel started the war in February, says Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia. "Today, the Islamic Republic's armed forces... having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war," Akraminia said, according to the state news agency Irna. "They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence." Akraminia said that Iranian armed forces retained control over the Strait of Hormuz and that it would remain closed until the United States accepted Tehran's demands. items.title: US and Iran edge closer to potential breakthrough in talks to end war, Bloomberg reports
items.summary: US and Iran edge closer to potential breakthrough in talks to end war, Bloomberg reports The United States and Iran are moving closer to a possible breakthrough in efforts to end the war, with Tehran considering proposals on its nuclear programme that it had previously been unwilling to discuss, Bloomberg reported, citing a diplomat familiar with the talks. The diplomat said Iran was studying proposals on its nuclear activities presented by Qatar, the main mediator. Any concession could help to advance negotiations, which have stalled since the collapse of an interim agreement reached in June. Reuters and The New York Times have also previously reported on Iran’s willingness to compromise on the nuclear issue. US President Donald Trump spoke by phone with Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani about efforts to de-escalate the conflict and secure a comprehensive agreement, the emir’s office said on Friday. Qatari officials have been shuttling between Doha and Tehran to help bridge differences, including over Iran’s nuclear activities and the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

items.summary: US military says it disabled cargo vessel in Gulf of Oman A US military aircraft fired on and disabled a commercial vessel that tried to break the US naval blockade of Iran on Saturday, US Central Command (Centcom) said. The St Kitts and Nevis-flagged cargo ship had visited an Iranian port and was trying to leave regional waters when a US plane fired precision munitions at its stern, after US forces ordered the crew to clear the targeted areas of the vessel, Centcom said. The US military also said on Saturday it was launching a task force to crack down on Iran’s movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material across its land borders and through the Caspian Sea, expanding on its months-long naval blockade. Centcom estimated that the blockade had prevented Iran from exporting more than $25bn worth of crude oil.

items.title: Aipac spent $55m on losing congressional candidates in midterm elections: Report
items.summary: Aipac spent $55m on losing congressional candidates in midterm elections: Report The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac) spent more than $84m in the 2026 US midterms, but nearly two-thirds of those funds were spent on losing candidates, according to a new report from Responsible Statecraft. Aipac’s Super Pac and other groups spent $55m on failed candidates. The largest portion of those funds, about $32m, was spent trying to defeat Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan. The results marked one of Aipac’s worst performances in years, suggesting that the US-Israeli war on Iran, which has contributed to soaring cost-of-living issues, resonated strongly with voters. In the 2022 midterms, Aipac’s Super Pac, United Democracy Project, saw 69 percent of its expenditure spent on races backed by the organisation that won. That number was even higher in 2024, after Israel’s genocide in Gaza, with 87 percent of its spending going to successful races. items.title: AIPAC dumped more than $55 million into losing midterm races
items.summary: The largest pro-Israel group in the U.S., the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC), has been silent on social media since Tuesday afternoon, well before polls closed across the country and Democrats won both chambers of Congress in a blue wave, largely driven by dissatisfaction over rising costs sparked by the war in Iran. The group was an early supporter of the war and a major funder of ads attacking House and Senate candidates calling to cut off aid to Israel. It spent big on the 2026 midterm elections, dumping $84.1 million via its super PAC, United Democracy Project (UDP), and several other PACs into races that have been decided as of this writing. AIPAC might be silent today because they need to explain to their donors how nearly-two-thirds, or $55.3 million, of that spending went to races in which the group’s preferred candidate lost. items.title: Trump extends shipping law waiver for 90 days amid Iran war fuel price rise
items.summary: Trump extends shipping law waiver for 90 days amid Iran war fuel price rise US President Donald Trump has extended by 90 days a waiver of a shipping law so that foreign-flagged ships can transport oil and other commodities between US ports, a White House official said on Friday. The administration would extend the waiver of the more than 100-year-old Jones Act, Reuters reported, citing industry sources. The administration issued a blanket waiver in March, a month after the US launched its war on Iran, in an effort to lower oil and fuel prices. When it extended the waiver in August, it said it would decide cases on a case-by-case basis, a condition that also applies to the latest extension. The Jones Act requires cargo moving between US ports to be carried on ships built in the US, owned by US companies, and crewed by American workers. The waiver aims to lower gasoline, diesel, and fertiliser prices, which have risen because of the war. items.summary: BRUSSELS, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Belgian Interior Minister Bernard Quintin said Iran was "very likely" behind the recent refrigerator cyberattacks on European shops, while Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot said there was insufficient evidence to draw conclusions. "There was enough evidence from our security services for me to say that Iran is very likely behind the cyberattacks we have seen targeting our shops," Quintin told Belgian broadcaster VRT NWS Thursday evening. Quintin made similar comments earlier on Thursday, but Prévot struck a more cautious tone.

items.title: Snoh Aalegra: Legendary Love review – raw R&B talent restrained by reverence for the greats
items.summary: (Stem) Her truly remarkable, Sade-ish voice is hypnotic against some dizzyingly plush production, but a modern spin on 80s pastiche sometimes veers too close to tribute Swedish-Iranian singer Snoh Aalegra has previously described her music – a lush, pastiche-y mix of R&B, hip-hop, soul and pop – as “cinematic soul”. But although she’s a dab hand at graceful, timeless presentation (and has a truly remarkable voice) Aalegra’s music has often struggled to match up to its aesthetic, hampered by her love of the greats and a penchant for broadly generic lyrics. Her most recent album, 2021’s Temporary Highs in the Violet Skies , made some headway toward carving out a more distinctive sound, thanks to sparky and inventive production from Tyler, the Creator, No ID, P2J and the Neptunes, but still didn’t quite feel like the right fit. items.title: Trump ran on a platform of peace. His war may have cost Republicans the midterms | Mohamad Bazzi
items.summary: Voters remembered Trump’s many promises to avoid the same kind of regime-change wars started by his predecessors For much of his political career, Donald Trump ranted at past US presidents who got the US entangled in endless foreign conflicts. items.summary: Saudi Arabia faces liquidity crunch even as oil exports rebound to pre-war levels Saudi Arabia is feeling the pinch of a liquidity crisis as bank deposits slow and the economy comes under pressure from the US-Israeli war on Iran, a new report from Bank of America says. In a note to clients, Bank of America said Saudi Arabia is grappling with “contagion” caused by liquidity tightness in the UAE and a rapid slowdown in the kingdom’s own economy, according to an article published on Bloomberg on Tuesday. The report said Saudi banks are feeling the pain in the UAE, which is also grappling with fallout from the Iran war and tighter liquidity. Saudi banks are closely linked to their Emirati neighbours, with a high number of interbank transactions contributing to deposits at Saudi banks. clusters.headline: 9/11 vets: Do politicians take  the decision to go to war seriously?

items.title: 9/11 vets: Do politicians take  the decision to go to war seriously?
items.summary: It is Veterans Day again, which means that, alongside the free red, white, and blue pancake specials and complimentary coffees, Americans will post tributes honoring the ultimate sacrifice of our soldiers. Just as predictably, on Memorial Day, veterans will receive well-intentioned messages thanking them for their service. Of course, Memorial Day honors those who died while serving in the U.S. military, whereas Veterans Day recognizes all who have served. This confusion is hardly something to get worked up about in itself. But it is symptomatic of something more consequential: a nation detached from its military and the wars it fights. In a sense, Americans are not wrong to conflate the two holidays. Service and sacrifice cannot be neatly separated, especially when the military has become an instrument of statecraft, diplomacy, humanitarian assistance, and lethal force whose deployment increasingly depends less on congressional authorization than on the decisions of a single president. Hij stelde dat de oorlog tegen Iran en de gevangenname van de Venezolaanse president Maduro niet zonder toestemming van het Congres hadden mogen plaatsvinden. Maar het voorstel van Massie strandde. De Republikeinen behaalden een meerderheid in het huis met 211 tegen 204 stemmen. clusters.headline: Are Democrats ready to make the most of the blue wave?

items.title: Are Democrats ready to make the most of the blue wave?
items.summary: Unless you’ve been living under a rock (no shame Patrick Star!), you’ve likely heard about last Tuesday’s “Blue Wave” midterm elections . The Democrats’ strong performance at the polls flipped control of the House and the Senate, delivering stunning results on the way, including flipping long-time red states like Kansas and Texas. As the GOP scrambles to repair the damage and Democrats strategize about how to use their new power in a divided Washington, one takeaway seems obvious: this was a foreign policy election, in which the Iran war and the costs it brought home served as the tipping point. But can we read these election results as a repudiation of U.S. foreign policy writ-large, or is this a specific response to one of the dumbest interventions in the long history of American adventurism? What does JD Vance's day-after effort to distance himself from the war tell us about how Republicans are digesting this result? clusters.headline: Israeli nuclear weapons, 2026

items.title: Israeli nuclear weapons, 2026
items.summary: Israel's longstanding policy of nuclear ambiguity ("amimut"), combined with severe intelligence restrictions and historical deception, continues to obscure the exact details of its undeclared nuclear arsenal. Despite these open-source research challenges, technical assessments suggest Israel maintains a strategic stockpile of roughly 90 single-stage, boosted fission warheads. This force is deployable across a triad of air, land, and sea delivery systems—including F-15/F-16/F-35 aircraft, Jericho ballistic missiles, and modified Dolphin-class submarines—even as US policy faces mounting domestic political pressure to abandon its decades-long refusal to acknowledge Israel's nuclear capability.

items.title: Qatar says US and Iran have responded positively to mediation
items.summary: Qatar says US and Iran have responded positively to mediation Qatar says Washington and Tehran have both responded positively to efforts to mediate between them. Doha is “working tirelessly to end the uncertainty over the crisis between Washington and Tehran”, the Qatari Foreign Ministry said. At his weekly briefing, the ministry’s media and communications director, Ibrahim bin Sultan al-Hashmi, said mediation was continuing. He added that the prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the onset of winter were doubling the cost of the crisis. Al-Hashmi also condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and said Qatar backed all steps Riyadh took to protect its security and stability.

Het schip is op rechterlijk bevel aan de ketting gelegd, liet de havenautoriteit (MPA) weten in een verklaring aan de Singaporese media . Er werden geen verdere details gegeven over de reden hiervoor. "De crew aan boord maakt het naar verluidt goed en de schuldeisers treffen maatregelen om hun welzijn te waarborgen", aldus MPA. Er waren geen gasten meer aan boord. Het bedrijf achter het cruiseschip, Villa Vie Residences, heeft nog niet gereageerd. clusters.headline: Cuts, evictions, and job losses: A view from the trenches of climate science in 2026

items.title: Cuts, evictions, and job losses: A view from the trenches of climate science in 2026
items.summary: A researcher at Columbia University who studies atmospheric and climate science gives a first-hand account of what it is like to pursue this work in the Trump 2.0 era, when the foundations of American science are being profoundly shaken. The post-World War II traditions that have made American science so successful—generous funding, awarded based on merit via peer review; academic freedom; openness to foreign talent; and most of all, systems of funding and executing science that are largely run by scientists, rather than by politicians—are under siege. What comes next is still an open question.

clusters.headline: How water, energy, and climate are reshaping international security

items.title: How water, energy, and climate are reshaping international security
items.summary: Water, energy, and mineral resources have long played a role in influencing and inciting political, ideological, and economic violence. But this violence is now worsening, driven by growing population pressures, expanding economies, and a fracturing and reforming of political alliances — and the wars in Ukraine, Israel-Palestine, and Iran. One surprising result may be an unanticipated acceleration of the global transition away from fossil fuels.

So was media coverage, and public opinion. But Trump has legitimized and encouraged backsliding.

As Kotkin once put it, “It turns out not everything is Munich. items.title: From Rulemaker to Rulebreaker? The 2011 NSG Revision to the U.S.-Saudi Nuclear Deal
items.summary:
From Rulemaker to Rulebreaker? The 2011 NSG Revision to the U.S.-Saudi Nuclear Deal
Arms Control Now Blog
[email protected] Mon, 11/09/2026 - 15:40

For several decades, the United States and other advanced nuclear states have worked cooperatively to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons and the technologies and materials that can be used to produce them. In the years since, every U.S. president on both sides of the aisle have tried to advance those efforts. In alignment with these efforts, in 2011, the United States spearheaded an international effort to tighten restrictions on the transfer of sensitive nuclear technology that can be used to build nuclear weapons, helping strengthen a nonproliferation norm.

Little is known about the Shahid Kaveh unit, although analysts have long observed that the IRGC, which has a vast network of operations, had actively branched out into cyber warfare in recent years. FRANCE 24's Reza Sayah reports from Tehran.

items.title: France opens probe into Iranian cyber unit over fridge attacks
items.summary: France on Monday said Iran's Revolutionary Guards were behind "unprecedented" cyberattacks on supermarket fridges in the country last month, vowing sanctions on a European level against Tehran. Ze zouden brand hebben gesticht bij openbare voorzieningen en een elektriciteitsstation hebben beschadigd, wat tot stroomuitval in sommige gebieden zou hebben geleid. De mannen werden er ook van beschuldigd dat zij opdrachten uitvoerden voor Israël en de Verenigde Staten, aartsvijanden van Iran. items.title: Corporate Re-entry as an Indicator of the End of the “Age of Wars”
items.summary: Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 marked not only a military but also an economic turning point in the international order. The mass withdrawal of multinational corporations (MNCs) from Russia demonstrated that geopolitical risk had begun to outweigh the benefits of global economic interdependence. But if corporate exit is one indicator of the beginning of a new “age of wars”, the gradual return of MNCs could be an indicator of its eventual end. Corporate return should not, however, be measured as a binary variable of returned/not returned. It is better understood as a sequence of increasingly costly and difficult-to-reverse commitments. This paper proposes a “corporate re-entry ladder” ranging from renewed institutional contacts and market reconnaissance to direct commercial presence and, ultimately, irreversible capital investment. items.summary: Centcom sets up 'Task Force Iron Gate' to disrupt Iran’s weapons transfers The United States Central Command (Centcom) has directed the establishment of a task force that will support US government's efforts to prevent Iran from using ground routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials. In a statement issued on Saturday on X, Centcom said Admiral Brad Cooper has directed the formation of Task Force Iron Gate, an internal staff of approximately 20 civilian and military personnel based in Tampa, Florida. It will coordinate with other US government agencies on preventing the movement of advanced weapons systems, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials, and "illegal revenue streams" across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea, Centcom added. "The establishment of Task Force Iron Gate reinforces the success of our ironclad blockade against Iran at sea," said Cooper. items.summary: In Israël mag oppositieleider Gadi Eisenkot (Yashar) als eerste proberen om een nieuwe regering te vormen. President Herzog heeft hem aangewezen als eerste formateur. De Likud-partij van Netanyahu was bij de verkiezingen dan wel de grootste, maar Eisenkot kreeg meer aanbevelingen van de partijen. Er zijn meerdere wegen die naar een regering kunnen leiden, maar eenvoudig wordt het niet. De Arabische partijen - de Verenigde Arabische Lijst (Ra'am) en de Gezamenlijke Lijst - hebben deze verkiezingen een recordaantal van negentien zetels gehaald. Zij kunnen Eisenkot aan een regering helpen, maar meerdere leiders uit het oppositieblok sluiten zo'n samenwerking uit. clusters.headline: IRGC spokesman announces lifting of restrictions on Iranian missiles

items.title: IRGC spokesman announces lifting of restrictions on Iranian missiles
items.summary: IRGC spokesman announces lifting of restrictions on Iranian missiles Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards has said that it has lifted restrictions on the range of Iran's missiles. IRGC spokesman, Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi reportedly made the comments at a press conference on Saturday, in response to question regarding the country's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei's warning to the US against further attacks on the country. Khamenei had previously said during a meeting with senior military commanders, that any renewed US or Israeli attck would be met with "with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response". The leader also reportedly ordered an update of Iran's military target database. According to Tasnim news agency, Mohebbi was asked on Saturday whether Khamenei's comments meant that limits on the range of Iranian missiles had been removed. He responded : "This restriction has been lifted for us". “Our duty is to show our capabilities on the battlefield,” he added.

items.title: Voormalig Midden-Oostencorrespondent Thomas Loudon (56) overleden
items.summary: Journalist en oud-correspondent Thomas Loudon is overleden. Hij kampte met neuro-endocriene tumoren (NET), een langzaam groeiende vorm van kanker. Vorig jaar kreeg hij de diagnose en deze week overleed hij daaraan. Hij was 56 jaar. In 2001 werd Loudon de eerste Nederlandse (video)journalist die zich na de Islamitische Revolutie in Iran vestigde. Hij deed in diverse talen verslag van ontwikkelingen in Iran, Afghanistan en het noorden van Irak voor onder meer de NOS, Trouw en Elsevier, maar ook voor buitenlandse media als CNN, het Chileense Canal 13 en Asia TV in Singapore. Egypte en Jordanië In 2003 trok hij naar de Egyptische hoofdstad Caïro, waar hij Midden-Oostencorrespondent werd voor de NOS. Daarna deed hij dat vanuit Jordanië. Hij maakte onder meer verhalen over de Amerikaanse oorlog in Irak. Correspondent bleef hij tot begin 2007, waarna hij terugkeerde naar Nederland. In de jaren daarna was hij actief als docent journalistiek in Groningen en Rotterdam. Ook richtte hij zijn eigen organisatie op om journalisten te ondersteunen in landen waar de persvrijheid onder druk staat. Daa

items.summary: Acts of greyzone aggression aim to spread panic. Europe has to show the saboteurs that we are resilient It was as though a ghostly hand had switched the settings on supermarket freezers across Europe from “freeze” to “defrost”. From Finland to Ireland, they suddenly began heating up , many reaching 50C and food worth millions of euros had to be thrown away. But no actual hand was needed to cause the meltdown. This was a cyber-attack, or rather a chain of attacks. Like pretty much everything else in 2026, supermarket freezers are digitally enabled. That makes them smarter and more efficient, but like everything else that is connected to the internet, it also makes them more vulnerable. Russian hacktivists claimed they were behind some of the supermarket sabotage, but no one knows for sure. It could also be Iran, Iranian proxies, North Korea – or unaffiliated bedroom hackers. items.summary: Iran demands US action, says it will not accept commitments on paper Iran will not rely on US commitments on paper as it considers entering a new diplomatic phase with Washington, Ali Baqeri, deputy secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, has said, according to Fars news agency. Referring to four rounds of negotiations over the past 18 months, Baqeri said Tehran believed the United States had derailed each round through hostile actions and breaches of commitments. “We must see practical actions on the part of the Americans,” he said, describing such steps as necessary before a new chapter in diplomacy could begin. Baqeri also discussed Iran’s cooperation with Russia, saying a recent visit by Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei to Moscow was intended to convey a message from Iran’s leader to President Vladimir Putin.

This debate raged through the historic MAGA coalition that brought Donald Trump and JD Vance to the White House. My position on it was clear: the war was the catalyst for my resignation from the Trump administration — and likely for many others who left without making their disagreement public. This debate burned hot and loudly in right wing circles online, on podcasts and occasionally even on right-wing mainstream platforms like Fox News. Then suddenly, on Tuesday night, after months of deafening argument, all of that debate was suddenly silenced, like a father coming home from work telling bickering siblings to knock off the racket. items.title: When the 'Watergate Babies' rode their own wave of anger
items.summary: If foreign-policy restrainers of both parties are looking for a model the new Congress can follow once it takes office in January, they could do worse than to refer back to the 1974 midterm election that brought to Washington a tidal wave of young Democrats who quickly passed legislation placing unprecedented constraints on the power of the “Imperial Presidency,” which had reached its zenith under former President Richard Nixon. In many respects, the parallels between the 1974 midterms and the results of Tuesday’s election are eerie. Though Nixon, whose own imperial pretensions were more sartorial than architectural , had resigned from office three months before the vote, his abuses of executive powers loomed large over the election. Those abuses were, after all, hard to ignore: from Watergate and the impoundment of Congressional appropriations at home, to the secret bombing of Cambodia and Laos and the covert CIA campaign to overthrow the democratically-elected government of Chile abroad. De grootste veranderingen zijn te zien onder jonge kiezers, mannelijke kiezers, Latino-kiezers en mensen met de middelbare school als hoogste opleidingsniveau. Dat zijn allemaal groepen die twee jaar geleden, tijdens de presidentsverkiezingen, nog massaal op Trump stemden . items.summary: From energy prices to datacenters, climate became a cost-of-living issue – and a winning one Climate-forward Democrats swept into power on Tuesday night as a blue tsunami flipped the Senate, House and several governor’s races. Voters were laser-focused on affordability, and experts said Democrats succeeded in linking cost-of-living concerns with rising energy prices, datacenters and, to some extent, the climate crisis. They may have even created a path for a “new climate politics”. The results delivered a sharp rebuke of Donald Trump, who started a war with Iran that raised gas pump prices across the country and exposed the fragility of fossil fuels, all while the US oil industry earned $130bn in profits since the war began. items.title: US issues fresh sanctions against individuals and entities aiding Iran
items.summary: US issues fresh sanctions against individuals and entities aiding Iran The US Treasury issued fresh sanctions on Wednesday targeting what it called "the vast criminal network" of companies and individuals tied to Iran. It named Indian nationals Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, as well as two other Indian citizens who head two of the couple's businesses, and nine separate entities connected to Sharma. "Their schemes have provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum, including vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies," the department said in a statement. The department also sanctioned Turkey-based Fugo Group Services Inc for its ongoing support of Iran's heavily sanctioned aviation sector.

The administration would extend the waiver of the more than 100-year-old Jones Act, Reuters reported, citing industry sources. When it extended the waiver in August, it said it would decide cases on a case-by-case basis, a condition that also applies to the latest extension. The Jones Act requires cargo moving between US ports to be carried on ships built in the US, owned by US companies, and crewed by American workers. The waiver aims to lower gasoline, diesel, and fertiliser prices, which have risen because of the war. items.summary: (Stem) Her truly remarkable, Sade-ish voice is hypnotic against some dizzyingly plush production, but a modern spin on 80s pastiche sometimes veers too close to tribute Swedish-Iranian singer Snoh Aalegra has previously described her music – a lush, pastiche-y mix of R&B, hip-hop, soul and pop – as “cinematic soul”. But although she’s a dab hand at graceful, timeless presentation (and has a truly remarkable voice) Aalegra’s music has often struggled to match up to its aesthetic, hampered by her love of the greats and a penchant for broadly generic lyrics. Her most recent album, 2021’s Temporary Highs in the Violet Skies , made some headway toward carving out a more distinctive sound, thanks to sparky and inventive production from Tyler, the Creator, No ID, P2J and the Neptunes, but still didn’t quite feel like the right fit. items.title: Iran's Political Future and Prospects for Democracy
items.summary: Across Iran, women, workers, and ordinary citizens continue to challenge the Islamic Republic through protests, civil resistance, and defiance of government restrictions. Severe economic instability, international sanctions, and the costs of war have intensified pressure on the regime, raising concerns within its leadership about further domestic unrest. The prospect of a democratic Iran also raises fundamental questions about the country's nuclear ambitions, relations with Israel, and the future of regional security.

items.title: The Iran War: What Comes Next?
items.summary: Following two rounds of direct conflict with the United States and Israel, Iran has shifted its strategy from military confrontation to economic pressure through the Strait of Hormuz. While hardliners claim victory and seek greater regional influence, Iran faces severe inflation, a collapsing currency, and growing divisions within its leadership. With China playing an increasingly consequential role, the region faces competing visions of its future: economic cooperation and normalization or continued confrontation under Iran's regional ambitions.

items.title: Iran's Transformation: From US Ally to Adversary
items.summary: Iran's close ties with the United States and Israel once formed a cornerstone of American strategy in the Middle East. The 1979 Islamic Revolution marked a turning point, as the US embassy hostage crisis, economic sanctions, and the Islamic Republic's support for regional proxy groups deepened tensions with both countries. The regime's pursuit of nuclear capabilities and its opposition to secularism and religious pluralism further shaped its foreign policy and regional ambitions.

The report said Saudi banks are feeling the pain in the UAE, which is also grappling with fallout from the Iran war and tighter liquidity. Saudi banks are closely linked to their Emirati neighbours, with a high number of interbank transactions contributing to deposits at Saudi banks. At the same time, the Saudi economy is under strain and government entities are making withdrawals from Saudi banks. But loan demand is high, which is effectively raising the cost of Saudi money. The chamber voted 211 to 204 to refer the charges to the House Judiciary Committee, where they could remain indefinitely for the duration of this Congress’s term, essentially killing the resolution for now. The articles were spearheaded by Republican Thomas Massie and backed heavily by Democrats, accusing Hegseth of carrying out unlawful orders and waging unconstitutional wars in Iran and Venezuela. Notably, there were 18 representatives missing during the votes - seven Republicans and 11 Democrats. The Democrats missing included California's Nancy Pelosi; Michigan’s Haley Stevens; New York’s Laura Gillen; California’s Lou Correa; New Mexico’s Melanie Stansbury; and several others. "The recent criminal and illegal aggression against Iran by America and the Zionist regime... has inflicted severe damage on the environment, releasing massive quantities of pollutants and greenhouse gases into the atmosphere," Pezeshkian said. He told COP31 that US-Israeli attacks released 1.5 million tonnes of CO2 into the atmosphere and caused extensive damage to the environment. Attacks on the Asaluyeh gas field in Iran's south on 8 March alone "resulted in the emission of approximately 500,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide", he added, while "the deliberate strike on fuel depots near Tehran led to the release of another one million tonnes". items.title: 9/11 vets: Do politicians take  the decision to go to war seriously?
items.summary: It is Veterans Day again, which means that, alongside the free red, white, and blue pancake specials and complimentary coffees, Americans will post tributes honoring the ultimate sacrifice of our soldiers. Just as predictably, on Memorial Day, veterans will receive well-intentioned messages thanking them for their service. Of course, Memorial Day honors those who died while serving in the U.S. military, whereas Veterans Day recognizes all who have served. This confusion is hardly something to get worked up about in itself. But it is symptomatic of something more consequential: a nation detached from its military and the wars it fights. In a sense, Americans are not wrong to conflate the two holidays. Service and sacrifice cannot be neatly separated, especially when the military has become an instrument of statecraft, diplomacy, humanitarian assistance, and lethal force whose deployment increasingly depends less on congressional authorization than on the decisions of a single president. items.title: Are Democrats ready to make the most of the blue wave?
items.summary: Unless you’ve been living under a rock (no shame Patrick Star!), you’ve likely heard about last Tuesday’s “Blue Wave” midterm elections . The Democrats’ strong performance at the polls flipped control of the House and the Senate, delivering stunning results on the way, including flipping long-time red states like Kansas and Texas. As the GOP scrambles to repair the damage and Democrats strategize about how to use their new power in a divided Washington, one takeaway seems obvious: this was a foreign policy election, in which the Iran war and the costs it brought home served as the tipping point. But can we read these election results as a repudiation of U.S. foreign policy writ-large, or is this a specific response to one of the dumbest interventions in the long history of American adventurism? What does JD Vance's day-after effort to distance himself from the war tell us about how Republicans are digesting this result? items.summary: Israel's longstanding policy of nuclear ambiguity ("amimut"), combined with severe intelligence restrictions and historical deception, continues to obscure the exact details of its undeclared nuclear arsenal. Despite these open-source research challenges, technical assessments suggest Israel maintains a strategic stockpile of roughly 90 single-stage, boosted fission warheads. This force is deployable across a triad of air, land, and sea delivery systems—including F-15/F-16/F-35 aircraft, Jericho ballistic missiles, and modified Dolphin-class submarines—even as US policy faces mounting domestic political pressure to abandon its decades-long refusal to acknowledge Israel's nuclear capability.

items.title: Cuts, evictions, and job losses: A view from the trenches of climate science in 2026
items.summary: A researcher at Columbia University who studies atmospheric and climate science gives a first-hand account of what it is like to pursue this work in the Trump 2.0 era, when the foundations of American science are being profoundly shaken. The post-World War II traditions that have made American science so successful—generous funding, awarded based on merit via peer review; academic freedom; openness to foreign talent; and most of all, systems of funding and executing science that are largely run by scientists, rather than by politicians—are under siege. What comes next is still an open question.

items.title: How water, energy, and climate are reshaping international security
items.summary: Water, energy, and mineral resources have long played a role in influencing and inciting political, ideological, and economic violence. But this violence is now worsening, driven by growing population pressures, expanding economies, and a fracturing and reforming of political alliances — and the wars in Ukraine, Israel-Palestine, and Iran. One surprising result may be an unanticipated acceleration of the global transition away from fossil fuels.

items.title: Trump looms large over Australia’s climate agenda. But retreat was already underway

items.title: 'Junk history' and Swedish neutrality
items.summary: The historian Stephen Kotkin of Stanford’s Hoover Institution has penned an important new essay on the phenomenon of “junk history”: reductionist or plainly wrong interpretations of historical events that have little or no basis in empirical reality but are nevertheless “marshaled in policy debates as justification for action, up to launching wars.” The emblematic example, which has recently been used by advocates for the war with Iran, is the failure of British Prime Minister Neville Chamberlain to truly ensure “peace in our time” at Munich in 1938. As Kotkin once put it, “It turns out not everything is Munich. It turns out Munich wasn’t even Munich when you get down into the nitty-gritty details.” Another example of junk history is what many otherwise well-informed American observers think they know about Sweden’s conduct during World War II and the Cold War. items.summary: As part of an effort to keep Russia on the radar of African countries still struggling from some of the negative externalities of Russia’s continuing war in Ukraine, Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted African leaders in Moscow last week for the third Russia-Africa summit . Between October 28 and 29, Russian officials met with their African counterparts in high-level discussions covering a wide range of issues, primarily focused on continued security relations and opportunities for greater economic collaboration. Of course, Russian engagement with Africa isn’t new. The Russian paramilitary group Africa Corps has around 2,500 fighters on the continent, where it has formed relations with a number of African governments to fight armed groups in exchange for payment, including through access to commodities. items.title: A Fox Under a Pink Moon review – Iranian teen refugee paints boldly imaginative self-portrait
items.summary: Soraya Akhlaghi filmed her perilous flight from Iran and precarious new life over five years on her phone, reassembled here with yearning animations The world feels like an overwhelmingly forlorn place in this striking refugee self-portrait, shot on smartphone by Soraya Akhlaghi over five years and assembled remotely by co-director Mehrdad Oskouei. Fleeing a dead-end life as a Tehran maid, Soraya – who is just 16 at the beginning of the film – starts out at an Istanbul asylum centre. Most “games” – as border-crossing sorties with people-smugglers are euphemistically called – end in failure in the wilderness at the hands of hostile law enforcement officers. Soraya is hoping to join her mother, who left for Austria after the death of Soraya’s father when she was a child. She winds up back in the Iranian capital, with her violent husband. items.title: El 'milagro' de dos centímetros que rescató a Amira: una historia de amor entre la medicina y la tecnología
items.summary: Hay historias que empiezan mucho antes de que nazca un niño. La de Amira comenzó cuando todavía era un pequeño corazón latiendo en el interior de su madre y los médicos descubrieron que algo no iba bien. El suyo latía demasiado despacio. Una bradicardia severa -frecuencia cardíaca muy baja- amenazaba con detener el reloj antes incluso de que la vida hubiera comenzado.Hoy Amira tiene ocho meses. Está viva. Y lleva dentro un dispositivo de apenas dos centímetros, el marcapasos más pequeño del mundo, diseñado específicamente para que un corazón tan diminuto como el suyo pueda seguir latiendo. Detrás de esos dos centímetros de tecnología hay meses de trabajo, una doctora que decidió llamar a una puerta que parecía demasiado grande para escucharla, doce ingenieros trabajando contra el reloj, y un científico de 65 años que decidió aplazar su jubilación para intentar salvar a una niña a la que no conocía.Es también, sobre todo, una historia de encuentros. He warned that if the Trump administration chooses war, it will will "see our alert and battle-hardened Warriors rain down hell." In a separate post, the Foreign Ministry quoted Araghchi on X, warning, “There are some American targets in the region outside military bases that may be within range of Iranian strikes.” American voters have made their choice. Time for the White House to make its own. Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results. A witness told Reuters that they saw blown-out windows across several floors of the Aramco Tower, one of the tallest buildings in the capital's King Abdullah Financial District. The incident, which the ministry said caused limited damage, came after the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted two missiles fired by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis towards Riyadh. Aramco was not immediately available for comment, and there was no immediate statement from the Houthis. Multiple loud booms were heard in Riyadh earlier on Sunday, a Reuters witness said, shortly after Saudi Civil Defense issued an early-warning alert of a potential threat in the region. items.summary: In Iran zijn drie mannen geëxecuteerd voor hun rol bij anti-regime-protesten in Karaj, een stad ten westen van Teheran. Dat meldt staatspersbureau IRNA. De protesten kwamen begin dit jaar tot een kookpunt. Om deze een halt toe te brengen, richtten Iraanse autoriteiten en paramilitairen een bloedbad aan onder demonstranten. Naar schatting ruim 7000 betogers werden gedood , ook werden duizenden actievoerders vastgezet. De drie geëxecuteerde mannen, Hassan Dioband, Hamid Kazemi en Reza Zanganeh, hebben volgens Iraanse autoriteiten vuurwapens, granaten en molotovcocktails gebruikt bij demonstraties op 8 en 9 januari. Ze zouden brand hebben gesticht bij openbare voorzieningen en een elektriciteitsstation hebben beschadigd, wat tot stroomuitval in sommige gebieden zou hebben geleid. De mannen werden er ook van beschuldigd dat zij opdrachten uitvoerden voor Israël en de Verenigde Staten, aartsvijanden van Iran. Jaish al-Adl is an outlawed militant group in Sistan-Baluchistan province, which has long seen clashes between security forces and armed groups, including Sunni militants and members of the ethnic Baloch minority. The mass withdrawal of multinational corporations (MNCs) from Russia demonstrated that geopolitical risk had begun to outweigh the benefits of global economic interdependence. But if corporate exit is one indicator of the beginning of a new “age of wars”, the gradual return of MNCs could be an indicator of its eventual end. Corporate return should not, however, be measured as a binary variable of returned/not returned. It is better understood as a sequence of increasingly costly and difficult-to-reverse commitments. This paper proposes a “corporate re-entry ladder” ranging from renewed institutional contacts and market reconnaissance to direct commercial presence and, ultimately, irreversible capital investment. items.summary: US military says it disabled cargo vessel in Gulf of Oman A US military aircraft fired on and disabled a commercial vessel that tried to break the US naval blockade of Iran on Saturday, US Central Command (Centcom) said. The St Kitts and Nevis-flagged cargo ship had visited an Iranian port and was trying to leave regional waters when a US plane fired precision munitions at its stern, after US forces ordered the crew to clear the targeted areas of the vessel, Centcom said. The US military also said on Saturday it was launching a task force to crack down on Iran’s movement of advanced weapons and other sanctioned material across its land borders and through the Caspian Sea, expanding on its months-long naval blockade. Centcom estimated that the blockade had prevented Iran from exporting more than $25bn worth of crude oil.

IRGC spokesman announces lifting of restrictions on Iranian missiles
items.summary: IRGC spokesman announces lifting of restrictions on Iranian missiles Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards has said that it has lifted restrictions on the range of Iran's missiles. IRGC spokesman, Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi reportedly made the comments at a press conference on Saturday, in response to question regarding the country's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei's warning to the US against further attacks on the country. Khamenei had previously said during a meeting with senior military commanders, that any renewed US or Israeli attck would be met with "with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response". The leader also reportedly ordered an update of Iran's military target database. According to Tasnim news agency, Mohebbi was asked on Saturday whether Khamenei's comments meant that limits on the range of Iranian missiles had been removed. He responded : "This restriction has been lifted for us". “Our duty is to show our capabilities on the battlefield,” he added.

items.summary: Journalist en oud-correspondent Thomas Loudon is overleden. Hij kampte met neuro-endocriene tumoren (NET), een langzaam groeiende vorm van kanker. Vorig jaar kreeg hij de diagnose en deze week overleed hij daaraan. Hij was 56 jaar. In 2001 werd Loudon de eerste Nederlandse (video)journalist die zich na de Islamitische Revolutie in Iran vestigde. Hij deed in diverse talen verslag van ontwikkelingen in Iran, Afghanistan en het noorden van Irak voor onder meer de NOS, Trouw en Elsevier, maar ook voor buitenlandse media als CNN, het Chileense Canal 13 en Asia TV in Singapore. Egypte en Jordanië In 2003 trok hij naar de Egyptische hoofdstad Caïro, waar hij Midden-Oostencorrespondent werd voor de NOS. Daarna deed hij dat vanuit Jordanië. Hij maakte onder meer verhalen over de Amerikaanse oorlog in Irak. Correspondent bleef hij tot begin 2007, waarna hij terugkeerde naar Nederland. In de jaren daarna was hij actief als docent journalistiek in Groningen en Rotterdam. items.title: Freezer meltdowns and airline hoaxes are a taste of things to come. Hoping for the best is no longer an option | Elisabeth Braw
items.summary: Acts of greyzone aggression aim to spread panic. Europe has to show the saboteurs that we are resilient It was as though a ghostly hand had switched the settings on supermarket freezers across Europe from “freeze” to “defrost”. From Finland to Ireland, they suddenly began heating up , many reaching 50C and food worth millions of euros had to be thrown away. But no actual hand was needed to cause the meltdown. This was a cyber-attack, or rather a chain of attacks. Like pretty much everything else in 2026, supermarket freezers are digitally enabled. That makes them smarter and more efficient, but like everything else that is connected to the internet, it also makes them more vulnerable. Russian hacktivists claimed they were behind some of the supermarket sabotage, but no one knows for sure. It could also be Iran, Iranian proxies, North Korea – or unaffiliated bedroom hackers. When Transport for London suffered a devastating hack two years ago, the culprits turned out to be two British teenagers . Eight attacks occurred in the Strait of Hormuz and three in the Arabian Gulf, according to UKMTO's weekly overview. Of the 11 incidents, three vessels continued their voyages, five required assistance and three sank. A Panama-flagged supply vessel was also struck by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on 1 November and reportedly sank after a nearby merchant vessel rescued its crew. items.title: US and Iran edge closer to potential breakthrough in talks to end war, Bloomberg reports
items.summary: US and Iran edge closer to potential breakthrough in talks to end war, Bloomberg reports The United States and Iran are moving closer to a possible breakthrough in efforts to end the war, with Tehran considering proposals on its nuclear programme that it had previously been unwilling to discuss, Bloomberg reported, citing a diplomat familiar with the talks. The diplomat said Iran was studying proposals on its nuclear activities presented by Qatar, the main mediator. Any concession could help to advance negotiations, which have stalled since the collapse of an interim agreement reached in June. Reuters and The New York Times have also previously reported on Iran’s willingness to compromise on the nuclear issue. US President Donald Trump spoke by phone with Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani about efforts to de-escalate the conflict and secure a comprehensive agreement, the emir’s office said on Friday. Qatari officials have been shuttling between Doha and Tehran to help bridge differences, including over Iran’s nuclear activities and the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

Haji Deligani also described the US naval blockade of Iran as “a form of war”, warning that Iranian forces would attack “at the appropriate moment”. On Tuesday, Iran’s top military commander warned that the country’s armed forces would respond to any threat without “geographical limits”.

This debate raged through the historic MAGA coalition that brought Donald Trump and JD Vance to the White House. My position on it was clear: the war was the catalyst for my resignation from the Trump administration — and likely for many others who left without making their disagreement public. Then suddenly, on Tuesday night, after months of deafening argument, all of that debate was suddenly silenced, like a father coming home from work telling bickering siblings to knock off the racket. items.title: When the 'Watergate Babies' rode their own wave of anger
items.summary: If foreign-policy restrainers of both parties are looking for a model the new Congress can follow once it takes office in January, they could do worse than to refer back to the 1974 midterm election that brought to Washington a tidal wave of young Democrats who quickly passed legislation placing unprecedented constraints on the power of the “Imperial Presidency,” which had reached its zenith under former President Richard Nixon. In many respects, the parallels between the 1974 midterms and the results of Tuesday’s election are eerie. Though Nixon, whose own imperial pretensions were more sartorial than architectural , had resigned from office three months before the vote, his abuses of executive powers loomed large over the election. Those abuses were, after all, hard to ignore: from Watergate and the impoundment of Congressional appropriations at home, to the secret bombing of Cambodia and Laos and the covert CIA campaign to overthrow the democratically-elected government of Chile abroad. items.title: Aipac spent $55m on losing congressional candidates in midterm elections: Report
items.summary: Aipac spent $55m on losing congressional candidates in midterm elections: Report The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac) spent more than $84m in the 2026 US midterms, but nearly two-thirds of those funds were spent on losing candidates, according to a new report from Responsible Statecraft. Aipac’s Super Pac and other groups spent $55m on failed candidates. The largest portion of those funds, about $32m, was spent trying to defeat Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan. The results marked one of Aipac’s worst performances in years, suggesting that the US-Israeli war on Iran, which has contributed to soaring cost-of-living issues, resonated strongly with voters. In the 2022 midterms, Aipac’s Super Pac, United Democracy Project, saw 69 percent of its expenditure spent on races backed by the organisation that won. That number was even higher in 2024, after Israel’s genocide in Gaza, with 87 percent of its spending going to successful races. items.title: The Guardian view on the midterms and foreign policy: American voters spoke, and now the world waits anxiously | Editorial
items.summary: The Democrats have gained new powers to constrain Donald Trump. But the drubbing that Republicans received could yet prompt him to new excesses Donald Trump is a president without parallel, but history can still be instructive. Lame duck presidents often focus on foreign policy to escape domestic discontent and establish a legacy in an area where a hostile Congress offers less of an obstacle. Mr Trump, who was stunningly rebuffed by voters in Tuesday’s midterms , might seek satisfaction in construction projects, the 2028 presidential race and his family’s future. Or, amid the humiliation and with Republican critics growing louder, he could distract attention with fresh adventurism – perhaps escalating against Cuba – or more likely a vengeful new offensive against Iran. Mr Trump won’t put in the legwork or attention to detail demanded by, say, Bill Clinton’s push for lasting peace in the Middle East. items.title: Election was a check on Trump — and Biden — foreign policy
items.summary: There is no debate as to why Donald Trump and the Republican Party suffered a historic and humiliating defeat at the polls on Tuesday: it all comes down to the Iran war and the cost-of-living crisis it has brought about. But lost in the conversation is that this was not just a rejection of the Iran war. It was also a repudiation of the broader foreign policy that repeatedly gets the U.S. into wars — or into supporting the wars and war crimes of U.S. partners. In many contests on Tuesday, the U.S.-Israel relationship was on the ballot too, and it was rejected by Republicans and Democrats alike in favor of recentering priorities back to national interests, including ending the flow of military aid to Israel. Trump famously ran on a promise to end forever wars and not to start new ones. But he ended up listening to the Israeli Prime Minister and started a major war with Iran, even though a diplomatic deal was on the table that was objectively stronger than President Barack Obama’s deal . In comments carried by Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency, the Iranian authorities said that the vessel had halted its journey after the collision, adding that the tanker had “turned off its detection and navigation systems”. items.summary: It has long been claimed that Americans do not vote based on foreign policy, but the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections demonstrated the limits of this truism, with a large majority of voters rejecting the Iran War waged by the Trump administration. Even before the election, an October Fox News poll indicated that the Iran war and issues associated with it (inflation and gas prices) were among the top issues voters were concerned about. Exit polling published by NBC News showed 74% of voters saw the Iran war as a “crucial” or “major factor” in their vote, while 62% believed using force against Iran was the wrong decision. This apparently has come as a nasty surprise to the war’s biggest defenders and surrogates, who had assured their followers that this backlash would not happen. Some have admitted their errors, but many have not, and that split has rapidly produced a circular firing squad, with neocons aggressively turning on those in their ranks who have conceded the war was a mistake. items.title: AIPAC dumped more than $55 million into losing midterm races
items.summary: The largest pro-Israel group in the U.S., the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC), has been silent on social media since Tuesday afternoon, well before polls closed across the country and Democrats won both chambers of Congress in a blue wave, largely driven by dissatisfaction over rising costs sparked by the war in Iran. The group was an early supporter of the war and a major funder of ads attacking House and Senate candidates calling to cut off aid to Israel. It spent big on the 2026 midterm elections, dumping $84.1 million via its super PAC, United Democracy Project (UDP), and several other PACs into races that have been decided as of this writing. AIPAC might be silent today because they need to explain to their donors how nearly-two-thirds, or $55.3 million, of that spending went to races in which the group’s preferred candidate lost. items.title: US issues fresh sanctions against individuals and entities aiding Iran
items.summary: US issues fresh sanctions against individuals and entities aiding Iran The US Treasury issued fresh sanctions on Wednesday targeting what it called "the vast criminal network" of companies and individuals tied to Iran. It named Indian nationals Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, as well as two other Indian citizens who head two of the couple's businesses, and nine separate entities connected to Sharma. "Their schemes have provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum, including vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies," the department said in a statement. The department also sanctioned Turkey-based Fugo Group Services Inc for its ongoing support of Iran's heavily sanctioned aviation sector.

items.title: Trump admits Iran war caused election losses but ‘we had to do it’
items.summary: Trump admits Iran war caused election losses but ‘we had to do it’ US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that the Iran war was responsible for his Republican Party's resounding midterm election defeat. Asked whether he agreed with Vice President JD Vance earlier remarks that the Iran war was "the reason we lost", Trump told reporters outside the White House ballroom construction site that his comments were "largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term". "But at the same time, if I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again. Because long term, it's the only answer. You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon," he added. He also ruled out firing Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, saying "he's doing a very good job," despite his role in pushing for military action against Tehran. US President Donald Trump speaks to reporters before the construction site of the East Wing ballroom at the White House in Washington, DC, on 4 November 2026 (Mandel Ngan/AFP)
